text:
Marta: Heads up — after last night's TPM key rotation we have ~30 nodes in ap-southeast1 failing secureboot attestation, hitting provisioning queue.
Samir: seeing same in telemetry, nodes stuck at OOB state 'unverified' and not moving to PXE.
Marta: exact error in BMC logs: `tpm: pcr0 mismatch, boot-policy rejected`
Jen: omg. did the rotation include the new seed that was supposed to be backwards-compatible?
Samir: it did, but firmware older than 1.2.8 doesn't handle the seed-hash collision well — it toggles the secure-boot flag transiently and the node reboots into rescue.
Kai: quick mitigation: can we flip secure boot off over OOB for the affected rack and reprovision? That avoids mass PG drain.
Marta: yes but that'll need physical OOB or ipmitool commands. I can run a targeted change for 12 nodes.
Marta: running: `for n in $NODES; do ipmitool -H $n -U admin chassis bootdev pxe; ipmitool -H $n raw 0x30 0x70 0x66 0x00; done` (this clears the BMC flag per runbook)
Samir: thanks. ops-bot just posted a canary fail for eu-west-1 too but only 2 nodes.
ops-bot: deploy-canary: bmc-seed-rotation-check failed on 2 hosts in eu-west-1.
Jen: we should avoid flipping secure boot globally — causes security posture regression. Prefer targeted per-rack until firmware patch deployed.
Kai: agree. Samir, can you add an autoscaling override so customer traffic doesn't get shifted to Dedicated pools and blow our burst budget?
Samir: set temporary override: `POST /internal/scale-override {"region":"ap-southeast1","scale_delta":-20}` — will keep pods local. Note: this may increase tail latency for queued requests.
Marta: Ops update: I toggled secure boot on 12 nodes in rack-27 via OOB and reprovision started. 8 still failing — BMC reports TPM PCR mismatch on boot.
Jen: attach the BMC logs from one failing node please.
Marta: pasted snippet: `BMC: tpm_verify() err -22, secureboot state -> FAILED -> fallback none`
Kai: That code path was flagged in the 1.2.8 release notes as fixed, but looks like some vendor boards have delayed microcode. We need to map serials -> firmware and isolate delta.
oncall-robot: pager: ap-southeast1 oncall acknowledged.
Samir: short-term plan: 1) OOB flip secure boot only where we can reprovision fast 2) mark affected serials for forced firmware update 3) roll a canary firmware 1.2.9 to 3 racks 4) update runbook with `tpm seed` check.
Jen: long-term: vendor escalation for microcode, plus a gating check in rotation job to run a preflight that validates PCR digest compatibility.
Marta: coordinating with Field to schedule physical reboots for the 8 stubborn nodes tomorrow morning (low traffic window).
Kai: cost note from infra-finance chat — if we drain and rehome workloads into Dedicated for the day, we might trigger burst > commit and incur ~3k extra cost. Avoid if possible.
Samir: noted, will try to keep within capacity. If we must drain, we can prefer lower-cost instance types in cloud fallback and throttle non-critical batch jobs.
deploy-bot: rollback-policy: canary-firmware 1.2.8 -> 1.2.7 if 1.2.9 fails observed error rate > 1%.
Jen: please add a postmortem stub and link runbook edits. I'll own the postmortem.
Marta: thread summary: TPM seed rotation exposed vendor microcode bug toggling secureboot, blocking PXE. Mitigations: targeted OOB secureboot toggle, firmware canary roll, serial-level firmware updates, update rotation preflight.
Samir: will open support ticket with vendor (ref: TICKET-1423) and tag security/compliance.
Kai: thanks all. Tag me when the 1.2.9 canary is live so I can watch latency dashboards. :thumbsup:
